youtube.baslik: Why can't a speechreader tell pat, bat and mat apart? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: A group of speech sounds that look the same on the lips is called a viseme. For example, the lips close for all three sounds p, b and m, so words such as pat, bat and mat, or mom, Bob and pop, look almost the same on the lips. Words like these are called homophenes; they are told apart by context, or by the voicing and nasality information that hearing carries.
